decisions.title: Isolation of untrusted researcher code
decisions.note: AlphaLab provides safe research-execution interfaces and process orchestration; the isolation of untrusted researcher code is enforced by the host or deployment environment. A separate Python process alone is never represented as a secure sandbox.

decisions.title: Numerical precision and canonical serialization policy
decisions.note: A documented policy: deterministic calculations first, appropriate precision preserved, rounding only where numerical error analysis justifies it, cross-platform behaviour proved by reference tests. No arbitrary fixed rounding to conceal numerical differences. The policy is ADR-0058 (accepted 2026-11-14): identity-bearing values are computed on exact or correctly rounded paths only, every value is recorded at full precision, and nothing is rounded to make two hosts agree (TD-09).

technical_decisions.title: An unseeded identifier scope is isolated (DET-007)
technical_decisions.problem: id_scope(None) returned a null context, so a run started without a seed inside a seeded scope drew its identifiers from that scope's stream: the enclosing run's later identifiers depended on whether, and how much, a nested run had drawn.
technical_decisions.alternatives: (a) Keep inheriting and document it. (b) An unseeded scope installs its own uuid4 source. (c) An unseeded scope derives a child stream from the enclosing one.
technical_decisions.decision: (b): id_scope(None) installs use_id_source(id_source(None)), a uuid4 source of its own.
technical_decisions.rationale: A scope must draw nothing from the scope around it. (c) still advances or depends on the outer stream; (a) leaves a seeded run's identifiers hostage to unrelated code.
technical_decisions.compatibility: A seeded run's identifiers are unchanged, and the enclosing scope now mints exactly what it would have without the nested run. An unseeded run's identifiers were never reproducible. No recorded result_id, configuration_id, schema or format moves; the certificate's evidence is unchanged.
technical_decisions.record: CHANGELOG [4.3.0] Fixed; the ledger, once the package version admits v4.3.0 entries.
technical_decisions.tests: tests/regression/test_unseeded_scopes_are_isolated.py (backtest, replay and session drivers; nested, repeated, fresh-interpreter and parallel copy_context probes); mutation K01.

technical_decisions.title: Registries derive their identifiers (DET-007, plan D-54-7)
technical_decisions.problem: experiment_tracking.start_run and cloud_research.submit_research_job drew their identifiers from the ambient stream, so starting a run or queuing a job inside a seeded backtest moved that backtest's stream, and neither identifier could be recomputed from what was declared.
technical_decisions.alternatives: (a) A dedicated seeded stream per registry. (b) uuid5 over a canonical, scheme-tagged key of the declaration and its place in the registry (ADR-0016's pattern). (c) A content hash of the declaration alone.
technical_decisions.decision: (b), with schemes alphalab.experiment_run.v1 and alphalab.research_job.v1. A run's key holds its place (runs already held), name, canonical parameters, timestamp, parent and canonical tags. A job's key holds the cluster, its submission count, type, task path, priority and instant, and not its kwargs, which may be any objects with no canonical text.
technical_decisions.rationale: A derived identifier draws nothing and is recomputable anywhere. (c) collides when a declaration is repeated, and (a) still depends on the order in which unrelated registries are used.
technical_decisions.compatibility: New runs and jobs get UUID strings as before, now derived; identifiers already recorded are read as written. No recorded result_id, configuration_id, schema or format moves.
technical_decisions.record: CHANGELOG [4.3.0] Fixed; the ledger, once the package version admits v4.3.0 entries.
technical_decisions.tests: tests/regression/test_registries_derive_their_ids.py (12 tests); stress scenario registries (stress_v4_3.py); mutations K02 to K05.

technical_decisions.title: The HTTP transport opens http and https only (SEC-002)
technical_decisions.problem: HttpTransport.get handed any URL to urllib, which opens file:// (a local file read) and follows a redirect to ftp://.
technical_decisions.alternatives: (a) Document the risk. (b) Allow http and https, refuse a URL with no host, and check every redirect's scheme before urllib's own rules. (c) Allow https only.
technical_decisions.rationale: (a) leaves the file read open. (c) refuses loopback and plain-http providers that the transport legitimately serves.
technical_decisions.compatibility: A caller passing another scheme now gets an error before anything is opened. Reading another scheme was never a stated capability (SECURITY.md stated TLS only), so nothing documented changes.
technical_decisions.record: CHANGELOG [4.3.0] Security; SECURITY.md; the ledger, once the package version admits v4.3.0 entries.
technical_decisions.tests: tests/unit/marketdata/test_http_transport.py (15 tests against a loopback provider); mutations L01 to L04.

technical_decisions.title: Release artifacts held to their commit, and the build shown reproducible
technical_decisions.problem: The verification record named no commit, and nothing showed that the artifacts held the tagged source or that another builder could produce them (plan W.1, RQ-04, RQ-07).
technical_decisions.alternatives: (a) Record the commit only. (b) Also hold every archived file to the commit's object store. (c) (b), plus a rebuild from git archive of the commit, compared byte for byte.
technical_decisions.decision: (c). The default source is the checkout's HEAD. Outside a checkout the command fails rather than skip the check, after every path is checked. --no-source, for downloaded assets, records that the source was not checked, and no workflow may pass it.
technical_decisions.rationale: RQ-07 compares published assets with a rebuild, which needs byte reproducibility; a fresh rebuild of v4.2.1 was already byte-identical (W.1).
technical_decisions.compatibility: The command line gains --commit and --no-source. The workflows' commands are unchanged (their checkouts are git), and hosted CI passed with the check on 1593381.
technical_decisions.record: CHANGELOG [4.3.0] Added; ENGINEERING_GUIDELINES (Distributions); RELEASE_RUNBOOK step 7. ADR-0071 (M13) will cite it.
technical_decisions.tests: tests/regression/test_release_correspondence.py (14 tests on repositories made in the test); mutations N01 to N05.

technical_decisions.title: A release is developed under its own version
technical_decisions.problem: From M1 the programme changes the public API and records v4.3 findings, and the records that take them are keyed to the package version: the manifest and its history copy, the certificate, and the ledger guard. Since v4.2.1 the suite also held every commit to the release state. At 4.2.1, an API change would have rewritten history/4.2.1.json, the record of what 4.2.1 shipped, and a 4.3 ledger entry fails the guard.
technical_decisions.alternatives: (a) Stay at 4.2.1 and bump at the end, with gates red or records wrong meanwhile. (b) A PEP 440 development version, 4.3.0.dev0; every gate, artifact name and tag check assumes MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. (c) 4.3.0 everywhere at once; the README and INTEGRATION would name a current release, and download URLs, that do not exist until publication. (d) 4.3.0 in an explicit development state.
technical_decisions.decision: (d). The package and its records are 4.3.0, and the CHANGELOG leads with '# [4.3.0] - Unreleased'. release_preflight.development_problems (run by the suite) holds the tree to everything a release is held to but that heading's date, and the documents a reader installs from describe 4.2.1, the newest dated release, until the release commit. The release gate (release_preflight.py version) is unchanged and refuses the tree for the undated heading.
technical_decisions.rationale: Every commit stays green and truthful, and the gate that matters is untouched. No document ever names a release that cannot be installed, and no line calls 4.3.0 unreleased (DOC-013). The release commit is one explicit step that the suite verifies.
technical_decisions.compatibility: No identity moves: the engine keeps its version out of every identity, and the certificate moved only its release labels, its source digest and API-1's digest of the manifest file. running_engine() and dataset provenance record 4.3.0 for runs this tree makes, which is true. Preflight.yml expects 4.3.0, and its push route names work/v4.3.0-release; the development branch never triggers it (D-W1).
technical_decisions.record: CHANGELOG [4.3.0] Changed; ENGINEERING_GUIDELINES (Pull Requests); RELEASE_RUNBOOK (the release commit); docs/api/history/README.md; plan change PC-04.
technical_decisions.tests: tests/regression/test_release_preflight.py (development-tree, incoherent-tree and release-tree cases; the state-aware identity test); test_release_facing_versions.py and test_version_markers_agree.py, held to the documented release. Shown on a scratch clone with the version alone bumped: 29 version-keyed tests failed there, and no identity, fixture or evidence test.

technical_decisions.title: ADR-0053 revision 3: where a continuation is held to its schedule
technical_decisions.problem: R53-1 asks for a supplied schedule digest on run_snapshot.restore and restore_checkpoints, as FUT-041 does for the registry. A bare run snapshot records no binding, so the parameter would have nothing to check there, and a caller could believe a continuation was held to its schedule when it was not. A bare digest also drops the scheme it was computed under.
technical_decisions.alternatives: (a) Add schedule_digest to both restores, as written; on a bare snapshot it checks nothing. (b) Hold a chain by its own envelope (checkpoint schema 3), and a bare snapshot by the cursor given the binding its provenance records; pass a ScheduleBinding, not a digest. (c) Put the binding into the run snapshot; this moves identity, which is option B, 5.0.
technical_decisions.decision: (b): ScheduleCursor.start(expected=), checkpoint(schedule=) and restore_checkpoints(schedule_binding=) take a ScheduleBinding, and run_snapshot.restore gains nothing. VERIFIED needs a result whose own delivery record is read; a payload's or a chain's check answers DECLARED. ScheduleBinding and ScheduleVerification live in alphalab.runtime, beside RegistryVerification, since a checkpoint (runtime) records a binding and runtime may not import backtesting.
technical_decisions.rationale: Every check named is one that actually happens, the scheme is compared with the digest, and no package edge is added.
technical_decisions.compatibility: Additive only: keyword-only parameters defaulting to None on checkpoint, restore_checkpoints and ScheduleCursor.start. Version-2 chains are byte-identical and restore as before. No identity moves.
technical_decisions.record: docs/ADR/0053-run-and-input-provenance.md (Departures from the plan's text); CHANGELOG [4.3.0].

technical_decisions.title: Manifest provenance: what identity version 2 records, and where the unattested finding belongs
technical_decisions.problem: Three questions were left open. (1) D-53-3 asks for 'unchanged behaviour plus a finding' when no provenance is given, but a version-1 manifest can never cite provenance, so the finding would land on every manifest ever made, changing every assessment. (2) ADR-0052's migration step refused instruments=False under version 2, and instruments defaults to False, so a refusal cannot be told apart from the default. (3) Provenance carries the result id, an output; comparing it as an input would report a rerun that did not reproduce as one whose inputs differ.
technical_decisions.alternatives: (1) The finding on every manifest without provenance; only under version 2; or none. (2) Refuse instruments=False under version 2, or record the registry under version 2 whatever instruments says. (3) Compare provenance_id between original and rerun, or compare only the inputs it binds -- the schedule's and the registry's digests, which are already compared.
technical_decisions.decision: (1) The finding only under version 2, the contract that asks for provenance. (2) Version 2 records the registry the run held whatever instruments says. (3) provenance_id is not an input; a version-2 rerun of a version-1 original is compared by version 1's rules, and a detail line says so.
technical_decisions.rationale: Version-1 manifests, their assessments and the certificate's evidence stay exactly as they were (CR-53-7, CR-53-8). A version-2 producer is told what it did not attest, and an outcome names what actually differed.
technical_decisions.compatibility: Version 1 is unchanged in identity, verification, gaps and findings; version 2 is opt-in. ReproducibilityManifest, canonical_manifest_key and derive_manifest_id gain trailing fields and parameters with defaults, rendered only when given. A version-1 manifest is also stored as v4.2.1 stored it: ReproducibilityManifest projects without the two new fields while they hold their defaults, because an evidence store refuses another value under an identity it holds (the frozen v4.2.1 evidence store's test found the first draft writing them).
technical_decisions.record: docs/ADR/0053-run-and-input-provenance.md section 6; docs/ADR/0052 (status: accepted, option C, opt-in); CHANGELOG [4.3.0].

technical_decisions.title: Provenance refuses a binding of no schedule for a run that delivered observations
technical_decisions.problem: The delivery-record rule (REP-009) checks observations only when a schedule is named, because a manifest naming none for such a run has never been refused. Read the same way, forged provenance binding no schedule verified NONE_GIVEN for a run that delivered observations.
technical_decisions.alternatives: (a) Tighten the shared rule, which refuses a manifest_for_run call that succeeds today, a change in what a valid call computes. (b) A stricter rule for provenance alone, which is new API. (c) Leave it, and let NONE_GIVEN mean less than it says.
technical_decisions.decision: (b): run_provenance and verify_provenance refuse a binding of no schedule for a run whose record shows delivered observations; manifests keep the 4.x rule.
technical_decisions.rationale: The vocabulary must never claim more than the run's record allows, and an existing call's result must not change in a minor release.
technical_decisions.compatibility: No existing call changes; provenance is new in v4.3.

technical_decisions.title: ADR-0058: host independence by construction, not by rounding
technical_decisions.problem: Plan section H.1 proposed recording identity-bearing statistics as decimal strings rounded to twelve significant digits, so hosts whose libm differs in the last bit would agree. The owner's direction for G0 item 24 forbids arbitrary fixed rounding that conceals numerical differences, and rounding cannot make two hosts agree anyway: values a last bit apart that straddle a rounding boundary round to different strings at any number of digits.
technical_decisions.alternatives: (a) Twelve significant digits, as H.1 proposed. (b) Fewer digits, chosen per statistic, with the same boundary failure. (c) Three classes of result -- exact, correctly rounded, host libm -- with identities allowed over the first two only, every value recorded at full precision, class-3 values compared by tolerances derived from error analysis, and host independence proved by pinned reference tests on Linux and macOS.
technical_decisions.decision: (c), with the transcendental an identity needs computed on an exact or correctly rounded path instead, such as the stationary bootstrap's block lengths by integer comparison of hash-counter draws.
technical_decisions.rationale: It follows item 24's direction exactly, extends what REP-005 already does for run records, and makes cross-host equality a property a test proves rather than an outcome a rounding hopes for.
technical_decisions.compatibility: No existing identity or figure moves; LIM-005 stays a stated limitation, now a named class with a rule.
technical_decisions.record: docs/ADR/0058-numerical-foundation-host-independence-and-the-identity-of-an-estimate.md; plan change PC-02's reading of AC-37.
technical_decisions.tests: Each M2 module's pinned reference tests on CI's Linux and macOS cells (built in M2).

technical_decisions.title: ADR-0054: where the selection statistics live, and the bounds their required arguments take
technical_decisions.problem: R54-8 makes CSCV's S and the bootstrap's block length required and bounded, without saying how; the draft placed the statistics in research but left their numerical class and their bounds open.
technical_decisions.alternatives: (a) Defaults for S, q and B, which the draft's review refused. (b) Required arguments, unbounded. (c) Required arguments with stated bounds: S even, 2 <= S <= T and S <= 20 (C(20, 10) = 184,756 combinations), trimming of T declared; q >= 1, B >= 1 and the seed required; the adjusted PSR's lag count required.
technical_decisions.decision: (c), with the statistics pure in alphalab.research over common only, bootstrap positions from a hash-counter stream (class 1), p-values as exact fractions, RC, SPA and PBO class 2, and PSR, DSR, MinTRL and the adjusted PSR class 3, never in an identity.
technical_decisions.rationale: A bound makes a required argument's cost and meaning explicit; S above 20 makes CSCV's combinations impractical in pure Python, and nothing about the method needs more.
technical_decisions.compatibility: Additive: new modules and names; the existing PSR, DSR, expected maximum Sharpe and multiple-testing corrections unchanged.
technical_decisions.tests: The oracle suite built in M2 (exact-enumeration CSCV, closed forms, published examples).

technical_decisions.title: The core's linear algebra: one Cholesky, QL for the eigensystem, Jacobi for the SVD, and their conventions
technical_decisions.problem: ADR-0058 makes common.linalg the one authority for a symmetric eigensystem and a thin SVD with vectors, Cholesky and a pseudo-inverse, with caller tolerances (section 2) and class-2 arithmetic for anything that may enter an identity (section 3). The constrained optimizer's private Cholesky had to move without moving a portfolio, the plan budgets a 500 x 500 eigensystem at 30 s in pure Python, and the conventions every caller relies on were open: which triangle of a symmetric matrix is read, the sign of a vector, what a result says about its convergence.
technical_decisions.alternatives: Eigensystem: (a) cyclic Jacobi, accurate to high relative precision on graded matrices with one global stopping criterion, measured at 147.5 s for 500 x 500; (b) Householder tridiagonalization and implicit QL (tql2), backward stable with orthonormal vectors, measured at 20.7 s. SVD: one-sided Jacobi, or Golub-Kahan bidiagonalization and implicit QR. Cholesky: a new factorization, or the optimizer's moved verbatim. Symmetry: refuse an asymmetric input exactly, refuse it beyond a tolerance, or read one triangle as LAPACK does.
technical_decisions.decision: (b) for the eigensystem, with the split criterion |e_m| <= tolerance (|d_m| + |d_m+1|) and max_iterations per eigenvalue, both required; one-sided Jacobi for the SVD (max_sweeps required), whose accuracy the plan sets no budget against; the optimizer's Cholesky moved verbatim, quadratic._cholesky delegating and Black-Litterman calling it directly, the private solve removed; the lower triangle read; each eigenvector and right singular vector with its largest-magnitude component positive, the left vector following; a ConvergenceReport on every iterative result; + - * /, sqrt and fsum only, after an exact power-of-two scaling, with no math.hypot or pow in the new code.
technical_decisions.rationale: Only (b) meets the plan's budget, and its accuracy is the normwise accuracy every caller of an eigensystem relies on. The SVD keeps Jacobi's relative accuracy, and its cost is stated (240.8 s at 500 x 500) with speed left to the optional backends (ADR-0057, LIM-010). Reading one triangle is the convention every library uses and the one the optimizer's factorization already had, which Black-Litterman's view system, symmetric only to rounding, depends on; an exact refusal would have broken it, and a tolerance would be a policy nobody chose. A fixed sign makes a result reproducible bit for bit, so it can be pinned and, as a class-2 value, enter an estimate's identity.
technical_decisions.compatibility: Additive. No public name is removed; the optimizer's private _cholesky keeps its name and _cholesky_solve, private, is gone. Every factor, pivot ratio and solve is v4.2.1's float for float, so no portfolio, result_id or figure moves. alphalab.common exports one new name, ConvergenceReport (API manifest 2,800 to 2,801 exports). ADR-0058's class-2 row now names math.hypot, which CPython computes itself, held by a pinned test.

workstreams.title: Scientific computing and numerical foundations

items.item: ADR-0058 accepted: one authority, required tolerances, three numerical classes, precision by error analysis, the estimate's identity
common.distributions: special functions (log-gamma, incomplete gamma and beta) and the t, chi-squared, F, gamma, beta, binomial and Poisson distributions
common.linalg: symmetric eigensystem and thin SVD with vectors, pseudo-inverse; Cholesky as one authority
common.optimize and common.quadrature, with required tolerances and ConvergenceError
The Estimate type and its identity
One authority: ml.linalg and ml's splits delegate (GAP-48)

evidence: alphalab/common/distributions.py: Student's t, chi-squared, F, gamma, beta, binomial and Poisson, each with CDF, survival function and quantile, beside the normal; log-gamma, log-beta and the regularised incomplete gamma and beta functions; ConvergenceError. Survival functions computed directly; quantiles by Newton kept in a bisection bracket, stopping on a converged step or a narrow bracket. tests/unit/common/test_distributions.py (186 tests): exact oracles -- finite closed forms in 80-digit Decimal (t and chi-squared for even degrees of freedom, the Erlang and Poisson sums) and exact Fraction (binomial, integer-parameter beta, F through it) -- held within a tolerance from each formula's error bound (the log-gamma prefix's terms, ADR-0058 section 4); inverse identities against the exact CDFs; published tables at the digits they print; deep tails; refusals; ConvergenceError at the limit. Writing it found a remembered t quantile wrong in its 11th digit, a quantile search that could stall once converged (fixed), the existing normal_cdf's lost lower tail (NUM-017), and that the test's own decimal precision had leaked into the suite's shared context (fixed with local contexts). Whole suite: 11,301 passed.

NUM-017 fixed: normal_cdf's lower half by erfc, its upper half the standard library's value for value; within 1e-13 of an independent continued-fraction oracle to -37 (tests/regression/test_normal_cdf_keeps_its_lower_tail.py, 17 tests); the certificate's evidence unchanged, only its source digest moved. Whole suite 11,318 passed.

EXE-015 found while testing M2: plan_schedule's remainder ranking negated Decimals, which round to the caller's context, so a direct call allocated otherwise than a run. Fixed to compare exactly; runs unchanged (example 74's algorithms byte-identical under hostile contexts, the frozen algorithmic replays resume to their result_ids); exact apportionment is FUT-048 for 5.0.

common.linalg: cholesky (CholeskyFactor, NotPositiveDefiniteError), symmetric_eigensystem (Householder tridiagonalization and implicit QL), singular_value_decomposition (thin, one-sided Jacobi) and pseudo_inverse, each iterative one with a required tolerance and iteration limit and a ConvergenceReport (new, alphalab.common.convergence), computing with + - * /, sqrt and fsum after an exact power-of-two scaling. tests/unit/common/test_linalg_factorizations.py (108 tests): exact oracles (Sturm bisection in Decimal for Wilkinson's W21+ and W21-, whose closest eigenvalues are 1e-13 apart, and the second-difference matrix; 2 x 2 closed forms in 60-digit Decimal; exact Fraction inverses and the rank-one pseudo-inverse), Higham's bounds, the Krylov-Weinstein residual bound in exact Fraction arithmetic, the four Moore-Penrose conditions, exact scaling by 2^+-700, pinned values identical in every bit under CPython 3.12.4, 3.13.18 and 3.14.10 (and, since ADR-0058 section 6 makes least squares identity-bearing, pins for least_squares and singular_values, which use math.hypot). Cholesky is one authority: portfolio_optimizer.quadratic and Black-Litterman call it, and tests/regression/test_cholesky_moved_unchanged.py (85 tests) holds every factor, pivot ratio and solve to v4.2.1's copied code float for float, refusals included. Budget: a 500 x 500 eigensystem in 20.7 s against the plan's 30 s (cyclic Jacobi, measured first, took 147.5 s); benchmarks/benchmark_numerical_foundation.py reports it and gates growth per doubling at 12x.

authority.summary: The owner delegated implementation of the approved plan: technical and architectural decisions (the open G0 items included), commits and pushes to work/v4.3.0-development, maintaining Draft PR #22, and monitoring and fixing hosted CI, through M0-M13 and all 30 workstreams. Each significant decision is recorded with its problem, alternatives, rationale and compatibility consequences, in an ADR where it is architectural.
binding: AlphaLab stays a universal, strategy-agnostic quantitative research engine.
The core keeps zero mandatory runtime dependencies.
Optional numerical, statistical, ML and DL dependencies integrate separately through stable interfaces.
A separate process alone is not a secure sandbox.
The host or deployment environment enforces the isolation of untrusted research code.
Numerical precision follows error analysis, not arbitrary fixed rounding.
No silent change to a historical result_id, configuration_id, schema or persisted format.
No breaking change for convenience: stage it, migrate it, or hold it for 5.0.
forbidden: Publishing a v4.3.0 GitHub Release or a PyPI distribution.
Changing the v4.2.1 tag or release.
Disabling security controls or rulesets to bypass a failure.
